# fobos-sdr

> RigExpert Fobos SDR -- a USB wideband receive-only SDR

**Vendor:** RigExpert

Status: **untested** — catalogued from documented sources, not yet proven here.

**Not maintainer-verified**: nobody on this project has run this hardware yet. The two facts are recorded separately on purpose (D-027) — a correct recipe and a tested device are different claims.

## What it is

A USB software defined radio receiver from RigExpert, the Ukrainian maker of antenna analysers, with two families of firmware: the original, driven through libfobos, and an "agile" one with a fast frequency-scan mode, driven through libfobos-sdr-agile. Both libraries are receive-only: they set a frequency, gain and sample rate and read samples, and have no transmit call.

## What you can do with it

General wideband listening through any program that speaks SoapySDR (SDR++, GQRX, CubicSDR, GNU Radio) or the vendor's own tools. RigExpert's published figures are not repeated: coverage, sensitivity and dynamic range are unmeasured here, and D-027 keeps "the identifier is right" and "it was run here" apart.

## Setup

Install the `libfobos` and `soapysdr-module-fobos` units (the second pulls `libfobos-sdr-agile`, which it needs to build), run `hammunition hardware apply` to write the udev rule and add yourself to `plugdev`, and log out and back in. `fobos_devinfo` then lists boards on the original firmware and `SoapySDRUtil --find="driver=fobos"` should list the board. All three build into /usr/local on every target: no distribution packages them.

## Known problems

**Nothing was run against a board.** A board on one firmware is invisible to the other library: the same USB identifier, a different bcdDevice, and no error. The agile library's own four example programs are not installed. The units are builds from upstream commits (two are untagged pins), not packages. Hardware revision 3 and earlier need particular firmware per upstream's versions.txt and README; this is not measured.

## How it identifies itself

| USB id | What | Confirmed | Node |
|---|---|---|---|
| `16d0:132e` | Fobos SDR on original or agile firmware, told apart only by bcdDevice | yes | libusb |

## What is not yet known

Not owned, so no descriptor has been read. Unknown: the manufacturer and product strings and whether the board reports a per-unit serial; whether the agile firmware's bcdDevice (0x0101) and the original's (0x0000) are the only two a unit shows; and every behaviour past enumeration. The firmware difference is visible only in bcdDevice, which this catalog's udev binding cannot match on, so one rule serves both. Closing it needs a Fobos attached from an owner, once on each firmware if they have both; `scripts/identify-device.sh fobos-sdr` does it read-only, no root.

*Who can close it:* nobody on this project owns one — an operator who does can close it with one lsusb ([how](../contributing/hardware.md)).

## Access and permissions

Group membership required: `plugdev` — added at install, applies at next login.

The generated udev rule provides a `/dev/fobos-sdr` symlink, mode `0660`, group `plugdev`.

## Firmware modes

- **vendor_tool** — tooling: [`libfobos`](../packages/libfobos.md)
  The identifier does not change between firmware families; the descriptor's bcdDevice does (0x0000 original, 0x0101 agile), and libfobos and libfobos-sdr-agile each open only their own. `fobos_fwloader` from the libfobos unit writes firmware (its API is fobos_rx_write_firmware and fobos_rx_read_firmware, added in libfobos v.2.3.2). No separate bootloader or DFU identifier is recorded: none appears in either library's source, and whether one exists is part of the gap. Firmware writes were not run, and the firmware files are RigExpert's to download, not carried.
